email.job: Tell the full review story in a standalone email, then connect the judgment to guided support. Do not imply that the reviewed account belonged to an Accelerator member.
email.body:
Carmen, our Google Ads lead, had explained that her starting position was to leave competitor terms in. The client's team then supplied a reason that made sense for this particular venue: there was an actual comparison being made by couples.

Later in the review, they discussed another venue. The team member identified it as belonging to a different market and didn't see those couples considering their venue. Carmen agreed with excluding it.

The distinction came from what the client's team knew about the market, considered alongside the searches Carmen was reviewing.

**Another venue appearing in the account doesn't tell us whether its couples would also consider yours.**

Your team may hear about those alternatives directly. That is relevant information for an expert to understand before making a recommendation about competing venue searches.

We want our guidance to account for it. We bring the advertising expertise, while you and your team bring knowledge of the place, the market and the conversations you're having with couples.

That gives us a more meaningful basis for a decision than treating every other venue's name the same way.

If you want to remain involved in running your advertising with that kind of expert support, the Google Search Accelerator is built around a clear division of work: we build and launch your campaigns, and you run them with our experts beside you.

You keep a role in your advertising, with guidance that makes room for the knowledge you already have about your venue.
email.ending:
If there's a Google Ads decision you'd like expert support with, reply to this email and tell me a bit about what you're trying to solve.

Talk soon,
Whitney

reels.job: Face-to-camera retelling of the review. Keep the two contrasting venue contexts together. Use two Reels for this narrow moment; a third would repeat the same argument without adding a distinct creative door.

reels.script:
During a venue's Google Ads review, the client's team explained why a competing venue's name made sense there.

Carmen, our Google Ads lead, was looking through the searches with someone from the venue's team. And when a bigger venue came up, that team member explained that some couples who had looked at that venue had come to them instead.

So there was a reason to give that search some consideration. Those couples could be looking at both venues.

Then they discussed another venue. The client's team explained that it was in a different market and wasn't somewhere they saw their couples making that same comparison. Carmen agreed with excluding it.

That's what matters to us in a review like this. We bring the advertising expertise, and the client's team brings knowledge of the conversations they're having with couples.

We need both before making that call. A venue name can tell us what someone searched for, but it doesn't explain whether our client's venue is a realistic alternative for them.

We want our recommendation to reflect that distinction, rather than treating every competing venue as the same decision.

caption.body:
When you run your venue's Google Ads, you want expert input that takes the account seriously and understands the market around it. Your team may hear about alternatives couples considered that wouldn't be obvious from a venue name alone.

That context came into a review led by Carmen, our Google Ads lead. A member of the client's team explained that some couples who had looked at a bigger venue had come to them instead. Later in the discussion, they identified another venue as serving a different market, without the same overlap. Carmen agreed with the recommendation to exclude that one.

The useful distinction came from combining the searches with what the client's team knew. We weren't treating every other venue as an interchangeable competitor, and the local explanation had a place in Carmen's judgment.

That's the kind of expert support we believe venue owners should have: someone who can make an advertising recommendation while understanding why a particular comparison does, or doesn't, make sense for their couples.
caption.hook: Your team's conversations with couples belong in the advertising discussion.
caption.ending: We want the decision to fit the venue and its market, with the client's knowledge included in the reasoning.

caption.body:
You know your venue's place in the local market. You also hear which other places couples explored, and those conversations can add meaning to the searches appearing in your advertising account.

In one review, our Google Ads lead, Carmen, heard from the client's team that some couples who had looked at a bigger venue had come to them instead. That information gave the competing venue search a context worth taking into account. When a separate venue came up, the team explained that it belonged to another market and wasn't a comparable option for their couples. Carmen supported excluding it.

Our view of those searches needed to reflect the difference. The account brought the names into the discussion; the client's team explained the relationship between those places and their couples.

We bring expertise to the recommendation without assuming that a report contains everything there is to know about a venue's market. Expert guidance should give relevant local knowledge a meaningful place in the decision.
caption.hook: A venue can be different from yours and still be part of a couple's shortlist.
caption.ending: That is how we want to work with venue teams: understanding the comparison before recommending what to rule out.

In either case, we want your local knowledge in the conversation. If you'd like to work through a real advertising decision with an expert, DM us "ADS" and let's talk about it.

caption.body:
You can understand your local couples well and still want a specialist beside you when an advertising decision comes up. The useful relationship brings those perspectives together rather than asking one to stand in for the other.

During a search review, Carmen heard two different explanations from a member of the client's team. One venue had been considered by couples who also explored theirs. A second belonged to a market the team didn't see as overlapping with their own. Carmen's agreement with excluding the second reflected that distinction.

This is why we don't want to judge another venue's relevance from its name alone. The report provides a starting point for the discussion, while the client's team can explain a comparison the account doesn't spell out.

For an owner who stays involved in running their ads, that kind of collaboration matters. You bring knowledge of your venue and its couples; we bring the expertise to weigh it in the recommendation.
caption.hook: Expert guidance should leave room for what your venue team knows.
caption.ending: DM us "ADS" if you'd like to talk about the expert support that would fit the way you want to run your advertising.

intended_shift.do: Start a low-barrier conversation with WIA about a real Google Ads decision they want expert support with.
intended_shift.believe: Expert guidance should make room for the local knowledge their team brings, while still taking responsibility for the advertising recommendation.
intended_shift.understand: Another venue appearing in a search report does not, by itself, establish whether its couples would also consider their venue.

body.wia_perspective: We want the account data and your knowledge of local couples in the same conversation. Before we rule out searches for another venue, we need to understand whether those couples might also consider yours.

hooks.text: During a venue's Google Ads review, the client's team explained why a competing venue's name made sense there.
Should a competing venue's name automatically rule out a Google Ads search?
A search report shows venue names without explaining how couples compare them.

narrative_outline.main_point: We check competing venue searches against the client's knowledge of couples before recommending an exclusion.
narrative_outline.transformation: The reader sees WIA's expertise as judgment developed with relevant client context, rather than decisions made from venue names alone.
problems_desires_symptoms: The owner wants expert guidance without having their team's knowledge of local couples treated as incidental.
A venue name in the report can look straightforward until someone explains the actual comparison.
The reader wants recommendations grounded in their venue's market, rather than a blanket rule about competitors.

card.guardrail: Credit Carmen's review and Erin's local knowledge, and identify Erin only as part of the client's team (her role isn't stated in the call). Keep competitor names, price comparisons and booking claims out; develop this as a view of WIA's judgment, not a keyword tutorial.

offer_fit.offer: Google Search Accelerator, we build and launch your campaigns, and you run them with our experts beside you
offer_fit.calendar_note: Hold for the following week while the Accelerator is open. Use a low-barrier invitation about working through a real decision with an expert, without selling an audit or implying ongoing management.

reader_fit.why: The reader wants to keep running the account with specialists beside them, including guidance on decisions that require their own market knowledge.
reader_fit.buyer_statement: “For venues and wedding professionals who want to manage their own advertising without spending years figuring it out through trial and error.”

card.why_selected: This is the strongest office-hours moment because the client contributed something the account couldn't supply. The point is how WIA includes that knowledge, rather than how competitor keywords work.
card.wia_in_action: Carmen reviewed search terms with Erin from the client's team and asked what unfamiliar places represented. Erin distinguished nearby alternatives from a venue in a different market, and Carmen used that context in the review.
card.why_it_matters: A venue appearing in the same search report isn't automatically an alternative a couple would consider. Local knowledge belongs in that decision alongside the account data.
evidence_points: Carmen asked whether “Brownstone” was a competitor; Erin explained its local meaning and said the term could stay. (19:20–19:29)
Carmen described her default of leaving competitor terms in, and Erin explained that some couples had considered a larger nearby venue before considering theirs. (20:09–20:30)
Erin identified an unfamiliar venue as being in the Hamptons and said its couples wouldn't be considering their venue; Carmen agreed with excluding it. (21:40–22:05)
card.reader_takeaway: I want experts who ask what my couples actually compare before making that call.
verify_before_publishing: Confirm permission to use the anonymous search-review exchange with the client's team.

surprise_for_experienced_advertiser.reason: WIA's specialist asked the client's team to help interpret the market, rather than assuming the account report could answer which venues couples would genuinely compare.
